note: Russia, as the Russian Federation, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire, with the land of the other Soviet republics, walked back from 2026.

reviewed.why: Russia and the other fourteen republics of the former Soviet Union, with the land held by breakaway states (Chechnya, Transnistria, Abkhazia, South Ossetia, Nagorno-Karabakh) hatched

Cuts for land moved between Soviet republics after the war: the Estonian and Latvian border districts given to the Russian SFSR, and the Karachay and Chechen highlands given to the Georgian SSR from 1943-44 to 1957
Land outside the Soviet Union that Soviet forces held after the war: Finland (Porkkala), Denmark (Bornholm) and Iran, whose borders have not changed since 1945, and Manchuria with Port Arthur
Finland, whose borders moved with the Soviet Union in 1940 and 1944, and the cuts for land that changed hands between 1939 and 1946
Cuts for Soviet land held by Germany and Finland in 1941-44 that was only part of a region
The Baikonur Cosmodrome area, part of Kazakhstan, leased to Russia since 1994
Cuts for land moved between Soviet republics in the 1920s: Taganrog and Shakhty, Gomel and Rechytsa, Bobruisk, and the Khivan part of Karakalpakstan
Finland, the Baltic states, Belarus, Ukraine and Moldova from the Russian Revolution, drawn as states held at the end of each year
The Russian part of Poland (Congress Poland and Bialystok), from 1905 to today; the rest of Poland is not yet rebuilt
The Caucasus (Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, the North Caucasus, and Kars, Ardahan, Artvin and Igdir in Turkey), from the end of the Napoleonic wars

Cuts for the land that changed hands between 1856 and 1900: Southern Bessarabia, the northern Kurils, the Ussuri land, the Sixty-Four Villages and the Zaysan basin; and Alaska, Russian America until 1867
Cuts for the lower Amur (Qing until 1858) and the Kokand forts on the Syr Darya (until 1853)
